title: [target] relagent-apk: full-reverse (APK cross-validation for relagent)
body:
### Target ID

relagent-apk

### Target URL or domain

https://gitlab.com/RmMsr/relagent

### Purpose

full-reverse

### Authorization basis

Public open-source repository (BSD 2-Clause) - source-available reverse engineering for interoperability research in the operator's own fleet RE program. No accounts, no sessions, no third-party systems touched by this brief. The paired .APK cross-validation request is filed separately.

### Scope domains

gitlab.com

### Side effect

read

### State-changing authorization

no

### Probe budget

24

### Execution venue

remote-service

### Surfaces requested

github-issue, cli, jsonl, chat, http-facade

### Evidence expectation

reproduced

### Submitter Role{Moniker}

_No response_

### Notes for the dispatcher

APK REVERSE ENGINEERING for relagent (https://gitlab.com/RmMsr/relagent). The Android app is published via F-Droid and Google Play; obtain the published artifact, extract manifest, permissions, endpoints actually called, embedded providers/routes; then CROSS-VALIDATE against the source tree both directions (repo <-> APK): claims in source not present in the artifact, and behavior in the artifact not present in source, are the findings. Particular checks for this target: the '100% on your hardware / pure local' claim vs the artifact's actual network behavior, and the llama.cpp/Gemma bundling claims vs what ships. Extraction axes (owner, 2026-10-28): (1) providers + programmatic integrations (extracted set goes to the Providers lanes), (2) feature matrix + 'routes' used, (3) design cues, (4) interaction methods, (5) wrappers, (6) sign-up/sign-in + provider registration methods, (7) workflows, (8) tools. Self-discovery: classification + tagging are part of the recon output, not assumed going in. Standing owner requirements (2026-10-27): immediate telemetry (streaming/evented, NOT delayed batch exports) and full controls of the surface minus dangerous ops, wherever the target exposes a controllable surface.
